newsitem.title: FRANCE: Eurotunnel suspends shares, debt mediation ends.
newsitem.headline: Eurotunnel suspends shares, debt mediation ends.

text.p: Channel Tunnel operator Eurotunnel SA/Plc on Monday suspended trading in its shares in London, Paris and Brussels as the mandate for two court-appointed debt mediators was due to expire at midnight.
The troubled Anglo-French company has been struggling to negotiate a restructuring of some 72 billion francs of junior-ranked bank debt since it froze interest payments to banks a year ago.

A spokesman for a Paris commercial court confirmed the mandate for mediators Robert Badinter and Lord Wakeham expires at midnight on Monday (2200 GMT) and said any statement would only be made after that.

Court president Jean-Pierre Mattei appointed the mediators in February to help negotiate the restructuring and extended their term in June and August. A source close to the talks said last week their mandate had not not been expected to be continued.
Sources close to the talks said the court was meeting on Monday morning to consider the case and expected negotiations to continue even though the mediators were stepping down.

The London Times newspaper reported 26 agent bank lenders of Eurotunnel were meeting on Friday to look at the latest proposals for dealing with the company's mountain of debt. The report said the meeting would be the first after the end of the mandate for the two mediators.

Although an outline financial structure has been roughly agreed between Eurotunnel and its six leading lenders, they have been unable to agree pricing of an expected debt-for-equity conversion and convertible securities which would lighten its loan payments.
